q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
fact: Mercury completes an orbit around the Sun in just 88 days.

q: What is the name of the planet we live on?
fact: Earth is the only known planet to support life.

q: What is the Moon to Earth?
fact: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.

q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
fact: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on July 20, 1969.

q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
fact: Mars looks red because its surface is rich in iron oxide, or rust.

q: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
fact: Jupiter is so large that about 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

q: What star is at the center of our solar system?
fact: The Sun contains 99.8 percent of all the mass in the solar system.

q: Which planet is most famous for its wide, bright rings?
fact: Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice and rock particles.

q: How many planets are in our solar system?
fact: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, leaving eight planets.

q: What galaxy is our solar system part of?
fact: The Milky Way contains an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars.

q: Which instrument do astronomers use to observe distant stars?
fact: The first telescopes for astronomy were built in the early 1600s.

q: What causes day and night on Earth?
fact: Earth rotates once on its axis about every 24 hours.

q: About how long does Earth take to orbit the Sun once?
fact: Earth travels about 940 million kilometers during one orbit.

q: Which planet is often called the Morning Star?
fact: Venus is the brightest planet visible from Earth.

q: In what year did Apollo 11 land on the Moon?
fact: Apollo 11's lunar module was named Eagle.

q: In what year was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?
fact: Hubble orbits about 547 kilometers above Earth.

q: What does ISS stand for?
fact: The ISS has been continuously occupied since November 2000.

q: What was the first artificial satellite launched into space?
fact: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in 1957.

q: What is the largest moon in our solar system?
fact: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is even larger than the planet Mercury.

q: Which former planet is now classified as a dwarf planet?
fact: Pluto was considered the ninth planet from 1930 until 2006.

q: What does a light-year measure?
fact: One light-year is about 9.46 trillion kilometers.

q: Which element makes up most of the Sun?
fact: The Sun converts hydrogen into helium through nuclear fusion.

q: Who was the first woman in space?
fact: Valentina Tereshkova flew aboard Vostok 6 in 1963.

q: How many moons does Mars have?
fact: Mars's two small moons are named Phobos and Deimos.

q: What is a black hole?
a: A region where gravity is so strong that light cannot escape
A hole in the ozone layer
An empty part of a galaxy
fact: The boundary around a black hole is called the event horizon.

q: Which famous comet returns about every 76 years?
fact: Halley's Comet was last visible from Earth in 1986.

q: Where is the main asteroid belt located?
fact: The asteroid belt contains millions of rocky objects.

q: What is it called when the Moon is fully illuminated from Earth?
fact: A full Moon occurs when Earth is between the Sun and the Moon.

q: What is Earth's escape velocity, approximately?
fact: A spacecraft must reach escape velocity to leave Earth's gravity without further thrust.

q: What is the nearest star to Earth besides the Sun?
fact: Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away.

q: Who performed the first spacewalk?
fact: Alexei Leonov spent about 12 minutes outside Voskhod 2 in 1965.

q: In what year was Voyager 1 launched?
fact: Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth.

q: What is the largest volcano in the solar system?
fact: Olympus Mons is about two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.

q: About how hot is the surface of the Sun in Celsius?
fact: The Sun's core is far hotter, at about 15 million degrees Celsius.

q: What is the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape?
fact: Once anything crosses the event horizon, it cannot return.
